classification.difficultyReason: Combine three compass-directed displacements, then use a right triangle to calculate distance and a reverse bearing.

content.prompt: A hiker walks due south for $6\text{ km}$ then on a bearing of $270^\circ\text{T}$ for $10\text{ km}$ and finally due north for $15\text{ km}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the distance between the starting point and the finishing point. Give your answer to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
The final position is $10\text{ km}$ west and $15-6=9\text{ km}$ north of the starting point. By Pythagoras’ theorem,

$$\begin{align*}d^2&=10^2+9^2\\d^2&=181\\d&=\sqrt{181}\\d&\approx13.5\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate, to the nearest degree, the bearing of the starting point from the final position.

answer.worked:
From the final position, the starting point is $10\text{ km}$ east and $9\text{ km}$ south. Let $\theta$ be the angle east of south.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{10}{9}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{10}{9}\right).\end{align*}$$

The bearing is measured clockwise from north:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=180^\circ-\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{10}{9}\right)\\\text{Bearing}&\approx132^\circ\text{T}.\end{align*}$$
